subject: INCIDENT: 32 anonymous production accounts minted by my own test harnesses 2026-09-09
description: Recorded because the rule was broken and the record should say so. Between 20:00 and 21:59 UTC on 2026-09-09, repeated runs of _tools/hexos/nt1-full-qc.test.js and _tools/hexos/nt1-completable-as-user.test.js against hexworth.com created 32 REAL anonymous Firebase Auth accounts, plus real addScore/save() progress writes and real deliverFlag Cloud Function invocations. Counted from Auth creationTime: anonymous total 6357, of which 32 fall in that window, distributed 12 in hour 20 and 20 in hour 21 UTC. DISTINCT FROM TASK 372, do not conflate the counts: 372 is about LOAD-TIME anonymous sign-in by drive-by traffic (~6300 accounts, ~45/day). This is a different mechanism - explicit test-driven signInAnonymously plus a real callable - and a different fault, mine. It breaks the platform's hard rule that tests must not reach production, the rule that exists because an emulator run once fired live Discord webhooks for hours. Aggravating: tasks 372 and 377 are ABOUT anonymous accounts created without a human, and these harnesses were creating them by the dozen while measuring that. Chris flagged the hazard; I acknowledged it as an open question instead of resolving it, then shipped it. MITIGATED, NOT CLOSED: both harnesses now refuse to run without --allow-production. That is a speed bump, not a boundary - see the emulator task, which is the real fix. The 32 accounts are NOT to be deleted: see the cloud-deletion rule; they are indistinguishable in kind from the other 6300 and any cleanup is a separate, documented decision.
